scope: Professional reports, theses, project documentation and technical manuscripts produced as DOCX/PDF in the docx domain. Mandatory status comes from law, regulation, contract or institutional rules; verify the current edition.
legal_note: This file is research guidance, not legal advice. A standard becomes obligatory when a law, regulation, customer contract, procurement clause or university regulation references it. ISO 5966:1982 is withdrawn; it is listed because many older report templates still cite it.

typography.font_pairing_rule: One display/heading family plus one text family; confirm Vietnamese, CJK and Greek glyph coverage before delivery.
typography.hyphenation: off for headings; optional for justified body text with a language dictionary

accessibility.reading_order: single column or clearly ordered columns; avoid floating text boxes for body copy

standards.title: Information technology — Document description and processing languages — Office Open XML File Formats — Part 1: Fundamentals and Markup Language Reference
standards.mandatory_when: A contract, regulator or archive requires OOXML (DOCX/XLSX/PPTX) as the editable source format.
standards.controls: Package structure, WordprocessingML, SpreadsheetML, PresentationML, DrawingML, fields, styles, sections, tables and drawings.
standards.how_to_comply: Write valid OOXML parts, keep relationships consistent, validate the ZIP/XML, and preserve the package when patching. Word writes transitional OOXML by default; do not claim Strict conformance unless tested.

standards.title: Documentation — Numbering of divisions and subdivisions in written documents
standards.mandatory_when: The report style guide or contract requires numbered divisions; often cited by engineering and scientific report templates.
standards.controls: Arabic numerals, full stops between levels, no trailing full stop, hierarchical numbering (1, 1.1, 1.1.1).
standards.how_to_comply: Link a multilevel list to Heading 1–9 in Word; use lvlText %1 / %1.%2 (no trailing dot); keep numbering automatic so the TOC and cross-references see it.

standards.title: Documentation — Presentation of theses and similar documents
standards.mandatory_when: A university, research institute or contract requires the ISO thesis layout; many institutions override it with their own regulation.
standards.controls: Title page, front matter, table of contents, headings, illustrations, tables, references, appendices, page numbering and paper.
standards.how_to_comply: Use the institutional template first; where silent, apply ISO 7144 structure. Keep the cover, front matter, body, references and appendices in separate sections.

standards.title: Documentation — Presentation of scientific and technical reports
standards.mandatory_when: Legacy templates or older contracts still cite it. Do not present it as a current ISO requirement.
standards.controls: Report title page, contents, headings, illustrations, tables, references and appendices.
standards.how_to_comply: Use it as historical guidance only. Prefer ISO 7144, the customer style guide and the current ISO/IEC Directives.

standards.title: Information and documentation — Guidelines for bibliographic references and citations to information resources
standards.mandatory_when: The contract, journal or institution requires ISO 690; otherwise APA, IEEE, Chicago, Harvard or Vancouver may be specified.
standards.controls: Deterministic citation and reference output for monographs, articles, web resources, datasets and legal materials.
standards.how_to_comply: Pick one style and apply it consistently. Use hanging indents, ISO 8601 dates, DOI/URL with access date, and link in-text citations to the reference entry.

standards.title: Technical product documentation — Data fields in title blocks and document headers
standards.mandatory_when: Engineering drawings or technical product documents are exchanged under a contract that cites ISO 7200.
standards.controls: Document identifier, title, revision, date, author, owner, classification and page count fields.
standards.how_to_comply: Map the required fields into the Word header/footer or the drawing title block. Keep field names and lengths stable across the document set.

standards.title: Date and time — Representations for information interchange
standards.mandatory_when: International projects, data exchanges, audit trails and any document with dates that must be unambiguous.
standards.controls: Calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD), times, durations, intervals, UTC offsets and reduced precision.
standards.how_to_comply: Use YYYY-MM-DD in metadata and references; use an explicit time zone for timestamps; do not use locale-only dates such as 03/04/2026 without a month name.

standards.title: Quantities and units — Part 1: General
standards.mandatory_when: Scientific, engineering, financial or regulatory reports that state measured quantities.
standards.controls: Quantity symbols, unit symbols, prefixes, decimal sign, significant figures and quantity calculus.
standards.how_to_comply: Put units in column headers, not every cell; use a space between value and unit; use the decimal marker of the document language consistently; keep significant figures stable.

standards.title: Writing paper and certain classes of printed matter — Trimmed sizes — A and B series
standards.mandatory_when: Print production or a customer requires ISO A-series paper.
standards.controls: A4 (210 × 297 mm), A5, A3 and the B series.
standards.how_to_comply: Set A4 in Word page setup; keep margins and the text column stable; test the PDF at 100% scale.

standards.title: Technical product documentation — Lettering — Part 1: Currently used lettering
standards.mandatory_when: Engineering drawings and technical illustrations that must follow ISO lettering.
standards.controls: Legibility, character shapes, heights and stroke widths for technical lettering.
standards.how_to_comply: Use a technical sans-serif face at the specified height; do not use decorative or condensed display faces for dimensions and labels.

standards.title: Document management — Electronic document file format for long-term preservation — Part 4: Use of ISO 32000-2 (PDF/A-4)
standards.mandatory_when: National archives, courts, regulators or procurement require PDF/A for long-term preservation.
standards.controls: Embedded fonts, device-independent colour, no external dependencies, metadata and tagged structure.
standards.how_to_comply: Export a tagged PDF, embed all fonts, avoid transparency that the target PDF/A level forbids, and validate with veraPDF before submission.

standards.title: Document management applications — Electronic document file format enhancement for accessibility — Part 1: Use of ISO 32000-1 (PDF/UA-1)
standards.mandatory_when: Public-sector accessibility law, EN 301 549 procurement, or a customer accessibility clause cites PDF/UA.
standards.controls: Tagged structure, reading order, alternative text, language, table headers, bookmarks and metadata.
standards.how_to_comply: Author with real heading styles and alt text, export a tagged PDF, then validate the tag tree and reading order. A visually correct PDF is not necessarily PDF/UA.

standards.title: Information and documentation — Records management — Part 1: Concepts and principles
standards.mandatory_when: Records, audit files, quality records or regulated project documentation.
standards.controls: Authenticity, reliability, integrity, usability, retention, access and metadata.
standards.how_to_comply: Give each controlled document an identifier, version, owner, approval date, classification and retention rule; keep the audit trail and avoid overwriting approved records.

standards.title: Quality management systems — Requirements — Documented information
standards.status: check the current edition at iso.org before citing
standards.mandatory_when: A quality management system, supplier qualification or customer contract requires controlled documented information.
standards.controls: Creation, updating, identification, format, review, approval, availability, protection, retention and control of documented information.
standards.how_to_comply: Use a controlled template with document ID, revision, approval, change log and classification; keep distribution and retention records.

standards.title: Quality management systems — Guidance for documented information
standards.mandatory_when: Guidance for implementing ISO 9001 clause 7.5; not a certifiable requirement by itself.
standards.controls: Structure, content, review, approval, control and maintenance of documented information.
standards.how_to_comply: Define document types, owners, approval workflow and change control before writing; keep the document set small and usable.

standards.title: Information security, cybersecurity and privacy protection — Information security management systems — Requirements
standards.mandatory_when: A contract or regulation requires an ISMS; security-classified documents.
standards.controls: Documented information, classification, access control, supplier security, incident records and retention.
standards.how_to_comply: Mark classification in header/footer, restrict distribution, keep an access/retention matrix, and avoid putting sensitive details in document metadata.

standards.title: Project, programme and portfolio management — Guidance on project management
standards.mandatory_when: Large projects that require a documented management approach and stage reports.
standards.controls: Project governance, business case, plans, stage/phase reports, risk, issue, change and lessons-learned documentation.
standards.how_to_comply: Use the report structure the project management plan defines; align the document hierarchy with the project lifecycle and decision gates.

standards.title: Systems and software engineering — System life cycle processes
standards.mandatory_when: Systems engineering contracts and lifecycle documentation for complex products.
standards.controls: Technical processes, project processes, agreement processes and the information items they produce.
standards.how_to_comply: Map each deliverable to a lifecycle process and a decision gate; keep requirements, architecture, verification and validation records linked.

standards.title: Preparation of information for use (instructions for use) of products — Part 1: Principles and general requirements
standards.mandatory_when: Product safety law or a product-specific standard cites it; EU machinery and medical-device documentation often does.
standards.controls: Information for use, safety information, task orientation, language, readability, structure, illustrations and usability.
standards.how_to_comply: Write task-based instructions, put safety information before the task, keep warnings visually distinct, test with representative users, and use the required language(s).

standards.title: Translation services — Requirements for translation services / Post-editing of machine translation output
standards.mandatory_when: A multilingual deliverable is procured as a professional translation or post-edited MT service.
standards.controls: Competence, translation process, revision, review, project management and post-editing quality.
standards.how_to_comply: Freeze the source, provide terminology and style guides, require revision by a second linguist, and record the post-editing level.

standards.title: Terminology work — Principles and methods / Terminological entries in standards
standards.mandatory_when: Terminology-heavy standards, glossaries and multilingual projects.
standards.controls: Term formation, definitions, synonyms, scope notes and term entries.
standards.how_to_comply: Keep a project glossary with one preferred term per concept; define terms before first use; do not use synonyms as if they were different concepts.

standards.title: Country codes / Language codes / Currency codes
standards.mandatory_when: International data exchanges, country lists, language metadata and financial reports.
standards.controls: Two-letter country codes, language codes and three-letter currency codes.
standards.how_to_comply: Use ISO codes in metadata and tables; do not invent abbreviations; keep the code list version in the data dictionary.

standards.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2 / Accessibility requirements for ICT products and services
standards.status: current (WCAG 2.2 W3C Recommendation, 5 October 2023; EN 301 549 v3.2.1, 2021)
standards.mandatory_when: EU public-sector procurement, the European Accessibility Act, US Section 508, or a customer accessibility clause.
standards.controls: Perceivable, operable, understandable, robust content: contrast, alt text, headings, tables, keyboard, reading order and language.
standards.how_to_comply: Use real heading styles, alt text, table header rows, 4.5:1 text contrast (3:1 for large text and graphics), a document title and language. Export tagged PDF and test with a screen reader.

standards.title: Printing process control / PDF/X / Viewing conditions
standards.mandatory_when: Commercial print, colour-critical brand documents or print procurement.
standards.controls: Colour separation, ink limits, ICC profiles, PDF/X conformance and viewing conditions.
standards.how_to_comply: Use the printer's ICC profile, convert images to the target CMYK space, export PDF/X with bleed and trim marks, and proof under ISO 3664 viewing conditions.

rules.statement: A4 or Letter is set explicitly; margins leave at least 20 mm on every side.
Headings use built-in Heading 1–9 styles; no level jumps greater than one.
Numbered headings use a multilevel list linked to the heading styles, not typed numbers.
The table of contents is a TOC field with hyperlinks, not manually typed entries.
Figure and table numbers are SEQ fields; captions are bookmarked for cross-reference.
Every REF/PAGEREF target exists as a bookmark.
Report figures are inline, centred, aspect-preserving and no wider than the text column.
Every informative figure has alt text; decorative images are marked as decorative.
Photos are at least 150 PPI at final size (300 PPI for print); line art 600 PPI.
Table grid widths fit the text column; the table does not spill into the margin.
The header row repeats on every page and rows do not split across pages.
Table captions sit above the table; figure captions sit below the figure.
Cover has no header/footer; front matter uses roman numerals; body starts at 1.
Running headers use STYLEREF and page numbers use PAGE/NUMPAGES fields.
The document language is set (vi-VN or en-US) for proofing and accessibility.
Title, author, subject, keywords and classification are set in core properties.
Fields are refreshed before delivery; a dirty TOC is not a final deliverable.
One citation style is used consistently, with hanging indents and ISO 8601 dates.
Appendices follow the references, start on a new page and have their own A, A.1 numbering.
When PDF/A is required, fonts are embedded and the file validates with veraPDF.
When PDF/UA is required, the PDF has a tag tree, reading order, alt text and language.

OOXML.note: ECMA-376 is the publicly available OOXML specification; ISO/IEC 29500 is the ISO edition.

provenance.source: ISO catalogue pages, W3C WCAG 2.2, ECMA-376/ISO 29500, Microsoft Word field documentation; compiled by T039
provenance.licence: Derived metadata and thresholds; no ISO/W3C text redistributed. Verify the publisher edition before citing.
provenance.confidence: published + judgement; thresholds marked in rules
